head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:642 — `import` appends pending rows exactly as written. It only runs the generic validator, which accepts any legal transition chain, so it never checks that imported rows are still `open`/`proposed` with `decided_by: null`. A hand-written `decisions-pending.yaml` row with `status: decided`, `decided_by: operator`, a `cli:` ref and a `proposed -> decided` transition `by: operator:decisions-command` gets imported into the live ledger (reproduced: exit 0, the row lands `decided`/`operator`). This skips `/decisions confirm` entirely, which the whole design rests on. Import should refuse any row past `proposed`, any non-null `decided_by`, and any `operator:` transition.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:538 — `confirm` sets `decided_by` from the row's existing `decided_by_ref`, and the agent supplied that ref at creation (`new --answer-ref session:<id>#turn-N` is accepted for open and proposed rows at :332). An agent can therefore make its own proposal come out `decided_by: operator` whatever the operator answered. The operator's own `--answer-ref cli:<now>` is silently dropped whenever a ref already exists (reproduced). `decided_by: operator` should come from the confirm-time operator reference, not from text the agent wrote earlier.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:359 — the only gate on `confirm`, `reject`/`supersede` of a decided row, and `context --clear` is a caller-supplied string (`--recorded-by decisions-command`). The model can pass that string itself through Bash. `disable-model-invocation` on `/decisions` and the grep checks over skill bodies and `allowed-tools` (tests/unit/user-invoked-commands.bats, dec-write-lib.bats:547-563) don't stop that, so "an agent that could run them would confirm its own decisions" (commands/decisions.md:25-26) is still true. Together with the two findings above, nothing enforces operator-only attribution. At minimum, document that this is an honour-system marker. Better, bind confirm to something the model cannot produce, such as an interactive TTY prompt or a hook-enforced Bash deny rule.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:513 — `confirm` calls `derive_attribution`, which drops `--answer-ref` in any unattended context. The PRD-status signal alone (`**Status:** … autonomous`) does not block confirm (test at dec-write-lib.bats:354), so an operator confirming interactively gets `decided_by: agent` with `decided_by_ref: null` (reproduced). Worse, the WARN at :314 says "the row stays proposed … until /decisions confirm" while the row in fact becomes `decided`. Confirm should either refuse under any unattended signal, or keep the operator ref when only the PRD signal holds.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:441 — in an interactive session a row with no `--cycle` and no resolvable default cycle is written with `cycle: null` and no warning (the warning fires only when unattended). Every rendered "Decisions taken on your behalf" section filters on `--cycle` (render-templates.md:106, prd-template.md, sdd-template.md), so those rows are dropped, and `list --format md` (:694) then prints "_None: every decision in this run was the operator's._", which is false (reproduced). Render step 1 also derives the cycle from `ledger.json .active_cycle` while `default_cycle` (:361-374) prefers `.run/*state.json .cycle_id`, and a missing key renders as the literal `null`. Require a cycle on every write, or have the PR or appendix section list null-cycle rows instead of claiming "None".
head/.claude/skills/run-mode/resources/render-templates.md:104 — `jq -r '.active_cycle'` prints the string `null` when the key is absent, so step 2 runs `--cycle null`, matches no row, and step 4 emits the "every decision was the operator's" line instead of the "ledger unavailable" fallback. Use `// empty` and treat an empty cycle as an error.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:601 — once an agent-proposed replacement is rejected, the old decided row keeps `supersede_proposed_by` pointing at the rejected row forever. The append-only check (validate-artifact.sh:681) forbids clearing that field, so no agent can ever propose another supersede of that decision. The guard should ignore a `supersede_proposed_by` whose row is `rejected`, or reject should clear the field on the old row.
head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:852 — `tolower(c[st]) ~ /resolved/` also matches "Unresolved", so an Open Questions row still unresolved WARNs as "Resolved without a DEC id" (reproduced). Anchor the match (e.g. `^[[:space:]]*resolved[[:space:]]*$`).
head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:787 — the tag-to-row rule accepts any DEC row whose `source` merely contains the PRD's basename (`index($2, n)`). For the usual `prd.md`, a row sourced from `old-prd.md`, `archive/…/prd.md` or another cycle's PRD satisfies the check. Match the path or the `prd.md#` anchor, not a bare substring.
head/.gitignore:150 — the change re-includes `grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml` as tracked state but does not add the file. The writer refuses every live write without it (dec-write-lib.sh:271), and the suites read its header from the repo (dec-write-lib.bats:28, grimoire-index.bats:80, validate-artifact.bats:630) and assert it is tracked (dec-write-lib.bats:564). The base `.gitignore` ignored the path, so a clean checkout has no ledger. Ship the seeded ledger with its header in this PR, or make the tests and writer create it.
head/.loa.config.yaml.example:278 — the schema reference `grimoires/loa/sdd.md §3.1` (repeated at dec-write-lib.sh:5 and validate-artifact.sh:44 and :505) points at a gitignored file (`.gitignore:144` `grimoires/loa/sdd*.md`) that only exists in the author's checkout. Downstream users and reviewers cannot find the schema. Move it to a tracked doc, e.g. docs/architecture/decision-lineage.md, and reference that.
head/.loa.config.yaml.example:140 — the example now pins `pacing: rounds`, and "an explicit value always wins". Anyone who copies the example and sets `interview.mode: minimal` gets rounds instead of the documented minimal default `batch` (comment at :127, REFERENCE.md Mode Behavior Table). Leave the key commented out so the mode-dependent default applies.
head/.claude/commands/decisions.md:27 — the doc says the tests check that no other command or skill calls the operator-only operations, but `reject` (operator-only on decided rows) is in neither check (dec-write-lib.bats:548, user-invoked-commands.bats check_operator_ops), which only cover confirm, supersede and context --clear.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:739 — `--help` prints lines 2-45, which includes the code line `export LC_ALL=C` (line 45). It should be `2,44p`.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

content.text:
The PR can't merge as it stands: it lets decisions be recorded as operator-approved without the operator approving them, which is the main thing it promises to prevent. I wrote 14 findings to `/workspace/review.md`, ending with `Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED`.

**Ways around operator approval (the first three I reproduced on scratch ledgers):**
- **`import` takes pending rows as written.** A hand-written pending file with a row already marked `decided`, `decided_by: operator` imports into the live ledger with exit 0. It never goes through `/decisions confirm`.
- **`confirm` uses a ref the agent wrote earlier.** An agent can attach a `session:` ref when it creates a row. On confirm, that ref makes the row `decided_by: operator`, and the operator's own `cli:` ref is silently dropped.
- **Confirming while the PRD's status line says "autonomous" records the wrong voice.** The operator's ref is discarded and the row lands `decided_by: agent`. The warning printed says the row "stays proposed", but it actually becomes `decided`.
- **The "operator-only" gate is just a string.** `confirm` and the other operator-only operations check only `--recorded-by decisions-command`, which the model can pass itself from Bash. The command's frontmatter flag and the grep-based tests don't change that.

**Other correctness problems:**
- Rows written without a cycle get `cycle: null` with no warning in interactive sessions. Every rendered "Decisions taken on your behalf" section filters by cycle, so those rows vanish and the section claims "every decision was the operator's" (reproduced). The PR-body template also turns a missing `active_cycle` into the literal string `null`.
- If an agent-proposed replacement is rejected, no agent can ever propose another supersede for that decision, because the stale pointer can't be cleared under the append-only rule.
- The SDD Open Questions check treats "Unresolved" as "Resolved" (reproduced).
- The PRD tag check accepts any ledger row whose source merely contains the PRD's file name, so a row from `old-prd.md` counts.

**Repo and doc problems:**
- The `.gitignore` change re-includes `grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml`, but the file isn't in the PR. The writer and three test suites need it.
- The schema is referenced as `grimoires/loa/sdd.md §3.1`, which is a gitignored file nobody else will have.
- The example config hard-codes `pacing: rounds`, which overrides the documented `batch` default for minimal mode.
- Smaller items: the docs say the tests cover `reject` as operator-only but they don't, and `--help` prints one line of code.

The round checker, writer and validator suites all pass (13, 44 and 51 tests). To run them I had to stub `compat-lib.sh` and create an empty ledger, since neither is in the PR. The session-start surface and grimoire-index suites partly fail, but only because they need files outside the PR.
